examples.cn: 这个设计是她去年做的一把椅子的变体。

examples.en: Small variations in temperature can change the result.
examples.cn: 温度的细微变化就可能改变结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞一起」——威（风）瑞（雨）一起变，变化就来了：变化

root: 源自拉丁语动词 variare「改变」的名词形式 variatio，经古法语进入英语；同族词有 vary、variant、variety、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Variation covers a process, a measured gap, a new version, a piece of music and a fact of biology.
sensesIntro.cn: variation 涵盖一个过程、一个测得的差距、一个新版本、一段音乐和一条生物学事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same tune sung five times, each time a little different.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一首歌被唱了五遍，每遍都略有不同。

branches.en: PROCESS LINE: change happening over time.
branches.cn: 过程线：随时间发生的变化。

branches.en: SIZE LINE: how far the values sit apart.
branches.cn: 幅度线：数值之间差多少。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the same thing in a new dress.
branches.cn: 形式线：同一样东西换的新装。

branches.en: LIFE LINE: inherited differences in a species.
branches.cn: 生命线：种群中可遗传的差别。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variation is measured, difference is simply noticed.
branches.cn: 对照线：variation 要被测量，difference 只需被察觉。

intro.en: Variation is a root plus an action-noun ending; the whole vari- family shares that stem.
intro.cn: variation 是词根加表动作的名词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用这个词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are variare, to change, and -atio, the action noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件是 variare「改变」和表示动作名词的 -atio。

items.example: It shows the word in use.

definition_zh: 多样性、变化；种类、品种；（同一类的）若干不同事物；综艺节目
definition_en: a range of different kinds of the same thing, or one particular kind
core_image: 一个装满各色水果的篮子，每一样都不同，却都属于水果
scene: 菜市场的摊位上摆着十几种番茄，大小颜色各不相同。The shop sells a wide variety of teas from the mountains.
sceneCN: 这里 variety 是「种类」（第 2 个义项：某一类中的一种）；句意为这家店出售山上产的各种茶叶。满篮各色果实互不相同的样子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：多样性、变化；种类、品种；综艺节目

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，是本词的形容词形式
动词，义为「变化、不同」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」
名词，义为「变体、变种」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」

senses.title: A range of kinds
senses.titleCN: 多样性：许多不同种类的集合
senses.definition: many different kinds of the same general thing
senses.definitionCN: 同一大类下许多不同的种类
senses.example: The market offers a wide variety of fruit in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天市场上水果种类很多。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; variety is the pattern of many kinds together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；variety 就是多种东西并置的图案。

senses.title: One kind among many
senses.titleCN: 种类：其中的某一个品种
senses.definition: a particular kind within a larger group, often a plant or product
senses.definitionCN: 较大类别中的某一具体种类，常指植物或产品
senses.example: The shop sells a wide variety of teas from the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售山上产的各种茶叶。
senses.why: The collective word narrows to a single item: this variety here, not the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合名词收窄为单个个体：是这一个品种，不是全部。

senses.title: Lack of sameness
senses.definition: the quality of not being all the same, valued as interest
senses.definitionCN: 不一模一样的性质，被视为有趣可贵
senses.example: A little variety in the menu keeps the children interested.
senses.exampleCN: 菜单上有点变化能让孩子们保持兴趣。
senses.why: Here the word judges rather than lists: sameness is dull, variety is good.
senses.whyCN: 这里的这个词在做评价而不是在列举：单调乏味，多样才好。

senses.title: A music hall show
senses.titleCN: 综艺：由多种节目拼成的演出
senses.definition: a show of separate acts such as singing, dance and comedy
senses.definitionCN: 由歌唱、舞蹈、滑稽戏等独立节目拼成的演出
senses.example: The theatre still puts on a variety show every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院每到冬天仍上演综艺节目。
senses.why: A show of many acts is variety made visible: one stage, many kinds.
senses.whyCN: 多种节目同台就是可见的多样性：一个舞台，许多门类。

senses.title: A biological subspecies
senses.titleCN: 生物变种：人工培育或自然分化的品种
senses.definition: a group of plants or animals differing slightly from the species, such as a cultivated breed
senses.definitionCN: 与物种略有差异的动植物群体，如栽培品种
senses.example: This variety of apple ripens earlier than the others.
senses.exampleCN: 这个苹果品种比其他的成熟得早。
senses.why: Growers keep a stable set of traits and give it a name, and that named set is the variety.
senses.whyCN: 栽培者把一组稳定性状固定下来并给它命名，这个被命名的群体就是品种。

intro.en: Variety comes from Latin varietas through French, built on varius, meaning spotted or of many colours.
intro.cn: variety 经由法语来自拉丁语 varietas，词根 varius 意为斑驳的、多色的。

items.en: The adjective varius described skins, stones or animals marked with several colours.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述带多色斑纹的皮、石头或动物。

items.en: The noun varietas named diversity and difference, with the ending -tas for a state.
items.cn: 名词 varietas 指多样与差异，词尾 -tas 表示状态。

items.en: French carried variété into everyday use for the many kinds of a thing.
items.cn: 法语把 variété 带入日常使用，表示同一事物的许多种类。

items.en: English borrowed variety in the sixteenth century, first for diversity, then for a kind.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 variety，先表多样性，后表某一品种。

items.en: In the nineteenth century variety halls gave the word its show business sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪的杂耍剧院给了这个词演艺行业的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds words for range and for a single kind.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示范围与单一品种的词。

entries.definition: Of several kinds; the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」。

entries.definition: A change or a changed version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、变体」。

entries.definition: Something that changes; the technical cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」，技术性的近亲。

entries.definition: Difference among things, often used of people and species.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性」，常用于人群与物种。

entries.definition: The spread from one end to the other of a set.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「范围」，一套东西从头到尾的跨度。

entries.definition: A group of different things to choose from.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可供挑选的一组」，强调可挑选。

entries.definition: One kind of animal kept by people, closer to a single variety.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「品种」，更接近单个品种。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the basket-of-fruit core and phrases like a wide variety of.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「一篮果子」的意象与 a wide variety of 这类搭配。

normal.en: A variety of teas means many different teas, not one.
normal.cn: a variety of teas 指许多不同的茶，不是一种。

normal.en: Variety is the opposite of sameness in food, music and life.
normal.cn: variety 在食物、音乐和生活中都是「单调」的反面。

normal.en: A new variety of rice may ripen earlier than the old one.
normal.cn: 一个新稻种可能比旧的成熟得早。

normal.en: A variety show strings separate acts onto one stage.
normal.cn: variety show 把各种独立节目串在一个舞台上。

normal.en: Add variety to a routine and the routine stops feeling like a routine.
normal.cn: 给日常加点变化，日常就不再像日常。

abstract.en: The word holds both the whole and one piece of it: a variety of things, and the variety you picked.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时装下整体与一片：诸多种类，以及你选中的那一种。

abstract.en: Diversity is a pattern, not a list: it needs to be seen from above.
abstract.cn: 多样性是一种图案而非清单：它需要从上方看才成形。

abstract.en: Sameness repeats, variety remembers: a varied diet and a varied life both stay alive longer.
abstract.cn: 单调只是重复，多样带着记忆：多样的饮食与多样的生活都活得更久。

examples.en: The library offers a variety of books for young readers.
examples.cn: 这家图书馆为小读者提供各种图书。

examples.en: We stayed at home for a variety of reasons.
examples.cn: 我们待在家里，原因有好几种。

examples.en: This variety of tomato grows well in cool weather.
examples.cn: 这个番茄品种在凉爽天气里长得很好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱提」——我瑞（锐）意爱提各种花样：多样性

root: 源自拉丁语名词 varietas（词根 varius「斑驳的、多样的」），经法语 variété 于十六世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Variety can mean many kinds together, one kind by itself, the pleasure of change, a stage show or a plant breed.
sensesIntro.cn: variety 可以指多种并存、单一品种、变化带来的趣味、综艺演出或植物品种。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of fruit where every piece is a different kind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只篮子，里面每个果子都是不同种类。

branches.en: SET LINE: many kinds seen together.
branches.cn: 集合线：许多种类放在一起看。

branches.en: ITEM LINE: one particular breed or kind.
branches.cn: 个体线：某一个具体品种。

branches.en: PLEASURE LINE: change that keeps things interesting.
branches.cn: 趣味线：让人保持新鲜的变化。

branches.en: STAGE LINE: many acts in one show.
branches.cn: 舞台线：一场演出里许多节目。

branches.en: CONTRAST: variety is the whole basket, a kind is one fruit.
branches.cn: 对照线：variety 是整篮，a kind 是一个果子。

intro.en: Variety is a Latin state noun; its family supplies the adjective, verb and technical forms.
intro.cn: variety 是拉丁语状态名词，它的家族还提供形容词、动词与技术形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pieces are varius, varietas and the adjective varius giving various.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁构件是 varius、varietas，而 various 直接来自 varius。

definition_zh: 各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的
definition_en: of several different kinds or several different people or things
core_image: 一排货架上摆着颜色形状各不相同的盒子，标签却写着同一类商品
scene: 聚会结束后，桌上留下了各色各样的杯子，高矮粗细都不相同。Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
sceneCN: 这里 various 是「各种各样的」（第 1 个义项：种类不止一种）；句意为整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。一排彼此不同的盒子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「以各种方式、不同地」
名词，义为「多样性、种类」，是本词的名词形式
动词，义为「变化、不同」
名词，义为「多样性」，较少使用
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: Of several kinds
senses.titleCN: 各种各样的：种类不止一个
senses.definition: of more than one kind, used before a plural noun
senses.definitionCN: 不止一种，用在复数名词前
senses.example: Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
senses.exampleCN: 整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; various names a set whose members do not match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；various 指成员彼此不一致的一组。

senses.title: Several and different
senses.titleCN: 好几个不同的：数量不定但都算在内
senses.definition: several different people or things, not exactly numbered
senses.definitionCN: 几个不同的人或物，数量不确切
senses.example: We met at various times during the year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们这一年里在不同时间见过几次。
senses.why: The word avoids giving a number; it counts only as far as several and no further.
senses.whyCN: 这个词回避给出具体数目：只数到「好几个」为止。

senses.title: From many sides
senses.titleCN: 多方面的：原因、来源各不相同
senses.definition: coming from many different sources or aspects
senses.definitionCN: 来自许多不同来源或方面
senses.example: The delay was due to various reasons, some of them personal.
senses.exampleCN: 延误有种种原因，其中一些是私人的。
senses.why: Each member of the set has its own origin; the word holds them side by side.
senses.whyCN: 这一组的每个成员各有来源，这个词把它们并排放着。

senses.title: Many-sided in skill
senses.titleCN: 多样化的：本事不止一样（较少用）
senses.definition: having many different abilities or forms, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 具有多种才能或形态，较旧的文学用法
senses.example: He is a various man, at home in both music and mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个多才之人，音乐和数学都能应付。
senses.why: The older sense applies the diversity to a single person, not to a group.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义把多样性用在一个人身上，而不是一群人身上。

intro.en: Various is the English form of Latin varius, spotted or mixed, with an adjective ending added on the way.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁语 varius「斑驳的、混杂的」在英语里的形态，途中加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: The adjective varius described things of mixed colour, uneven or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述颜色混杂、不齐整或多种多样的事物。

items.en: Its plural varii was used for several different people, close to the modern sense.
items.cn: 其复数 varii 用于指若干不同的人，很接近现代含义。

items.en: English formed various from the Latin stem, first meaning changeable or diverse.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出 various，最初意为易变的或多样的。

items.en: Modern usage settles it before plural nouns, meaning several different.
items.cn: 现代用法把它固定在复数名词前，表示好几个不同的。

items.en: The word now shares its family with variety, variable and vary, all from the same Latin stem.
items.cn: 它如今与 variety、variable、vary 共用一个家族，全部出自同一拉丁词干。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds quantifiers for a loose plurality.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示不确切多数的限定词。

entries.definition: The noun for many kinds or one kind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」。

entries.definition: The verb, to differ or change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「变化、不同」。

entries.definition: Made varied, not all alike; close to various in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，意义接近 various。

entries.definition: Able to change, or a symbol that varies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: More than two but not many, without the sense of unlike.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「几个」，不强调彼此不同。

entries.definition: Not the same as one another, the core of various.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不同的」，是 various 的核心义。

entries.definition: Of mixed kinds put together, often in a box or pack.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「什锦的、搭配好的」。

entries.definition: Many in number, with no emphasis on variety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「众多的」，不强调种类。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the prefix habit of various and real collocations such as for various reasons.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 various 只修饰复数的习惯，以及 for various reasons 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Various always sits before a plural noun: various reasons, never various reason.
normal.cn: various 总在复数名词前：various reasons，不能接单数。

normal.en: Various means more than one, but it refuses to say how many.
normal.cn: various 表示不止一个，却不肯说有几个。

normal.en: For various reasons is a polite way to avoid listing the reasons.
normal.cn: for various reasons 是避免一一列举的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied describes a thing, various describes a group of things.
normal.cn: varied 形容一样东西，various 形容一组东西。

normal.en: The same root gives variety, vary and variable.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还给出 variety、vary 与 variable。

abstract.en: Various is a quiet way of saying that a group refuses to be summed up in one word.
abstract.cn: various 是一个低调的说法：这一组无法用一个词概括。

abstract.en: The word is plural by nature; it draws its meaning from the gaps between members.
abstract.cn: 这个词天生带复数性：它的意思来自成员之间的差异。

abstract.en: Say various and you admit you have not checked everything, only that the pieces differ.
abstract.cn: 说 various 就等于承认你并未逐一核对，只确认了它们互不相同。

examples.en: Various people offered to help with the move.
examples.cn: 有好几个人主动提出帮忙搬家。

examples.en: The delay was caused by various problems with the engine.
examples.cn: 延误差是由发动机的种种问题造成的。

examples.en: Books on the subject are available in various languages.
examples.cn: 这个主题的书有各种语言的版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱死」——各式各样的东西我瑞（锐）意爱死：各种各样的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 varius「斑驳的、多种的」，经英语自造词 various 进入使用；同族词有 variety、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Various ranges from many kinds before a plural noun, to an unnumbered several, many sources, and an older sense of many-sided.
sensesIntro.cn: various 从复数名词前的「多种」，到不确切的好几个、多来源，以及较旧的「多才」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of boxes, same category, every shape and colour different.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排货架上的盒子同属一类，却个个形状颜色不同。

branches.en: KIND LINE: the members are not alike.
branches.cn: 种类线：成员彼此并不相同。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: several, with no exact number.
branches.cn: 计数线：好几个，不给具体数字。

branches.en: ORIGIN LINE: causes and sources differ.
branches.cn: 来源线：原因与出处各异。

branches.en: ABILITY LINE: one person with many sides.
branches.cn: 才能线：一个人有多面。

branches.en: CONTRAST: various refuses both one word and a fixed number.
branches.cn: 对照线：various 既不肯概括，也不肯给数。

intro.en: Various is a Latin stem with an English adjective ending; the whole vari- family shares the stem.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁词干加英语形容词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用该词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is varius; the plural varii already meant several different people.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 varius，其复数 varii 已经表示「若干不同的人」。

definition_zh: 变化；变动；使不同；各不相同；（随情况）改变
definition_en: to change, or to differ from one another
core_image: 同一把尺子量十个人，每量一次读数都不一样
scene: 山脚下是春天的花，爬到半山就只见残雪，山顶则冻得人发抖。Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
sceneCN: 这里 vary 是「各不相同、有差异」（第 2 个义项：彼此不同）；句意为同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。尺子每次读数都不一样，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：变化、变动；使不同；各不相同

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」
形容词，义为「各种各样的」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」
名词，义为「变化、差异」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: To change over time
senses.definition: to change in amount, level or form over time
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、水平或形式上随时间改变
senses.example: The water level varies with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 水位随季节变化。
senses.why: Latin variare means to make different; the verb follows whatever the changing thing does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为使不同；这个动词跟着变化者一起走。

senses.title: To differ from one another
senses.definition: to be different between individual cases
senses.definitionCN: 在各个个体之间有所不同
senses.example: Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。
senses.why: Here nothing changes over time; the differences exist side by side in one moment.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有随时间而变化，差别在同一时刻并排存在。

senses.title: To change deliberately
senses.titleCN: 主动改变：故意换个做法
senses.definition: to make something different on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意使某物不同
senses.example: He never varies his route to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他上班路线从不改变。
senses.why: The subject is a person here, and the change is a choice rather than a natural drift.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，变化是一种选择而不是自然漂移。

senses.title: To depend on something
senses.titleCN: 随……而变：跟着另一个因素走
senses.definition: to change according to another factor
senses.definitionCN: 随另一个因素改变
senses.example: Crop yields vary according to rainfall and soil.
senses.exampleCN: 作物产量随降雨与土壤而变化。
senses.why: The verb leaves the subject to someone else: yields follow the rain, and the rain decides.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把主导权交给别人：产量跟着雨水走，由雨水决定。

intro.en: Vary is the direct Latin verb variare, to make different, taken into English without an ending change.
intro.cn: vary 就是拉丁语动词 variare「使不同」几乎原样进入英语。

items.en: The adjective varius meant spotted, mixed or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的、多种多样的。

items.en: The verb variare meant to make different, to alternate or to diversify.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为使不同、交替变换、使多样化。

items.en: Old French variier softened the Latin verb and gave it a French shape.
items.cn: 古法语 variier 让拉丁动词软化，并赋予它法语形态。

items.en: English shortened it to vary in the fourteenth century, meaning to undergo change.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把它缩短为 vary，意为经历变化。

items.en: Modern English uses it both for changing and for differing, two sides of one Latin idea.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它表「变化」也表「不同」，这是同一个拉丁观念的两面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of shifting and differing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 vari- 家族；近义组收表示变化与不同的动词。

entries.definition: Of many kinds, the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干。

entries.definition: Many kinds or one kind; the noun of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」，同词干。

entries.definition: Something that changes, or a symbol for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: A change or difference in amount or form.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变化、差异」。

entries.definition: The plain verb for becoming different.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「改变」，最普通。

entries.definition: To be unlike, only the side of comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同」，只表示比较的一面。

entries.definition: To rise and fall again and again, like a level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动」，反复起落。

entries.definition: To move from one position or state to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「转移」，从一个位置或状态移到另一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the two faces of vary, changing and differing, with real phrases from news and shops.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用 vary 变化与不同这两面，搭配取自新闻与店铺的真实说法。

normal.en: Vary with time, differ from place to place: one word for both.
normal.cn: 随时间变叫 vary，各地不同也叫 vary：一个词两面用。

normal.en: Prices vary widely means the range is large.
normal.cn: prices vary widely 指差价范围很大。

normal.en: Vary in size means the sizes are not all the same.
normal.cn: vary in size 指大小并不一样。

normal.en: Opinions vary is a polite way of saying nobody agrees.
normal.cn: opinions vary 是「谁都不一致」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied is the adjective, variety the noun, varying the participle.
normal.cn: varied 是形容词，variety 是名词，varying 是分词。

abstract.en: Vary needs two reference points: a thing at two times, or two things at one time.
abstract.cn: vary 需要两个参照点：一样东西的两个时刻，或同一时刻的两样东西。

abstract.en: Change is motion, difference is structure; vary describes both with one shape.
abstract.cn: 变化是运动，差异是结构；vary 用一个形状描述两者。

abstract.en: A life without vary is a line, not a landscape.
abstract.cn: 没有变化的生活是一条线，不是一片风景。

examples.en: Prices vary widely between the two markets.
examples.cn: 两个市场的价格差别很大。

examples.en: Her mood varies with the weather.
examples.cn: 她的心情随天气变化。

examples.en: The recipes vary only in the amount of sugar used.
examples.cn: 这些食谱只是在用糖量上不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞」——威（风）瑞（雨）一来，天气就变：变化

root: 直接来自拉丁语动词 variare「使不同、变换」，经古法语 variier 于十四世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、variety、variable、variation。

sensesIntro.en: Vary covers change over time, difference between cases, deliberate change and dependence on a factor.
sensesIntro.cn: vary 涵盖随时间变化、个体间差异、主动改变与随因素而变四种情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler measuring ten people, with ten different readings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子量十个人，十次读数都不同。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the same thing is different later.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一样东西后来不同了。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: different cases at one moment.
branches.cn: 空间线：同一时刻的各个个体不同。

branches.en: WILL LINE: a person chooses to change.
branches.cn: 意志线：人主动选择改变。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: one factor pulls another along.
branches.cn: 因果线：一个因素带着另一个走。

branches.en: CONTRAST: change is one thing twice, vary also covers two things once.
branches.cn: 对照线：变化是一样东西的两次，vary 也含两样东西的一次。

intro.en: Vary is a bare Latin verb stem; its English relatives come from adding endings to the same root.
intro.cn: vary 是不带前缀的拉丁动词词干，英语亲属词都在同一词根上加词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is variare from varius; the English verb drops the ending entirely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是出自 varius 的 variare，英语动词整个去掉了词尾。

items.example: It forms varied and the past tense.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 varied 与过去式。

items.example: It is shared by the whole family.

definition_zh: 巨大的；广阔的；浩瀚的；大量的、极多的
definition_en: extremely large in area, amount or degree
core_image: 站在沙丘顶端望出去，地平线一直退到眼睛看不见的地方
scene: 夜里没有一盏灯，抬头只看见铺满星星的天。A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
sceneCN: 这里 vast 是「广阔的、浩瀚的」（第 1 个义项：面积极大）；句意为一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。地平线退到看不见的地方，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的、广阔的、浩瀚的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「极大地、远远地」，如 vastly improved
名词，义为「广阔、浩瀚」
名词，书面说法，义为「广袤」，较少使用

senses.title: Enormous in area
senses.titleCN: 面积巨大：眼睛望不到边
senses.definition: extremely large in area or extent
senses.definitionCN: 面积或范围极大
senses.example: A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。
senses.why: Latin vastus meant empty and desolate; the emptiness itself is what takes the breath away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vastus 意为空旷荒芜；正是这种空旷让人屏息。

senses.title: Enormous in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量巨大：多到难以清点
senses.definition: extremely large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目极大
senses.example: A vast amount of data was collected over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间收集了海量的数据。
senses.why: The word moves from space to quantity: numbers can also open out like a plain.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从空间移到数量：数字也能像平原一样铺开。

senses.title: Great in degree
senses.titleCN: 程度巨大：差别或优势悬殊
senses.definition: very great in degree, used of differences and advantages
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上非常大，用于差别与优势
senses.example: There is a vast difference between the two plans.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案之间差别巨大。
senses.why: Here the size is abstract: not metres but distance in quality or outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的大小是抽象的：量的是质量或结果上的距离，而非米数。

senses.title: The great majority
senses.titleCN: 绝大多数：人群中的绝大部分
senses.definition: used with majority to mean almost all
senses.definitionCN: 与 majority 连用，表示几乎全部
senses.example: The vast majority of students passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 绝大多数学生通过了考试。
senses.why: A crowd can be vast too; the same word measures people.
senses.whyCN: 人群也可以是 vast；同一个词也能量人。

intro.en: Vast comes from Latin vastus, empty and desolate, which already described land that stretched out bare.
intro.cn: vast 来自拉丁语 vastus「空旷荒芜的」，本已形容光秃秃铺展开的土地。

items.en: The adjective vastus meant empty, waste or desolate, applied to ruined land.
items.cn: 形容词 vastus 意为空旷的、荒废的、荒凉的，用于被毁坏的土地。

items.en: Its verb vastare meant to lay waste, and lies behind English waste and devastate.
items.cn: 其动词 vastare 意为摧残荒废，是英语 waste 与 devastate 的来源。

items.en: Old French vaste kept the sense of wide and unoccupied space.
items.cn: 古法语 vaste 保留了辽阔空旷的意思。

items.en: English borrowed vast in the fifteenth century for enormous extent.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 vast，表示范围极大。

items.en: Modern usage extends it from land to amounts and differences, while the sense of emptiness fades.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从土地扩展到数量与差别，同时「空旷」的感觉渐渐淡去。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of waste and emptiness; the near-meaning group holds words for great size.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「荒废、空」的拉丁词干；近义组收表示巨大的词。

entries.definition: By a very large amount; the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极大地」，是本词的副词形式。

entries.definition: The quality of being vast; the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广阔」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To lay waste or ruin; uses the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Empty or unused land; a distant English cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「荒地、浪费」，英语里的远亲。

entries.definition: Very large in size, plainer and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，更日常。

entries.definition: So large it cannot be measured; close in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边的」，语气接近。

entries.definition: Larger than normal, with a hint of shock.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「庞大的」，带惊奇感。

entries.definition: Having no limits, stressing no edge rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边无际的」，强调没有边界。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the empty-plain core and real collocations like vast majority.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「空旷平原」意象与 vast majority 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Vast majority means almost all, not merely most.
normal.cn: vast majority 指几乎全部，不只是大多数。

normal.en: Vast came from a Latin word for empty land.
normal.cn: vast 来自拉丁语中表示空地的词。

normal.en: Vast difference is a huge gap, not a big object.
normal.cn: vast difference 指巨大差距，不是巨大物件。

normal.en: Vaster and vastest exist, though writers often use more vast.
normal.cn: vaster 与 vastest 存在，但作家常用 more vast。

normal.en: Vastly improved means improved by a very large amount.
normal.cn: vastly improved 指改善幅度极大。

abstract.en: Vast began as emptiness and became size: the feeling of distance is older than the measure of it.
abstract.cn: vast 从「空」长成「大」：对距离的感受比测量更古老。

abstract.en: Something vast makes the viewer small, which is why the word always carries a trace of awe.
abstract.cn: 巨大之物让人显小，所以这个词总带一丝敬畏。

abstract.en: The same word measures land, data and differences, because largeness is a comparison, not a substance.
abstract.cn: 同一个词量土地、数据与差别，因为「大」是比较，不是实体。

examples.en: Vast areas of the country remain uninhabited.
examples.cn: 这个国家的大片地区仍无人居住。

examples.en: She spent a vast amount of time on the research.
examples.cn: 她在这项研究上花了大量时间。

examples.en: The vast majority of customers were satisfied.
examples.cn: 绝大多数顾客表示满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇死他」——哇，他一个人管那么大一片地：广阔的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 vastus「空旷荒芜的」及其动词 vastare「荒废」，经古法语 vaste 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 devastate、waste。

sensesIntro.en: Vast starts with land that has no edge, then measures quantities, differences and the bulk of a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: vast 从望不到边的土地开始，然后用来量数量、差别与人群的绝大部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizon that keeps moving back as you look at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：你越看，那条地平线退得越远。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: land and water without visible edge.
branches.cn: 空间线：看不见边际的陆地与水面。

branches.en: QUANTITY LINE: numbers or data in huge bulk.
branches.cn: 数量线：成堆的数字与数据。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: a gap that feels like distance.
branches.cn: 程度线：像距离一样的悬殊。

branches.en: CROWD LINE: nearly all the people counted.
branches.cn: 人群线：被计数的人几乎全部。

branches.en: CONTRAST: huge is a size, vast is a stretch.
branches.cn: 对照线：huge 指尺寸，vast 指铺展。

intro.en: Vast is a whole Latin stem; its English relatives take -ly and -ness, while devastate keeps the Latin verb.
intro.cn: vast 是完整的拉丁词干，英语亲属词接 -ly 与 -ness，而 devastate 保留拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair is the adjective vastus and the verb vastare, both about emptiness and ruin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的一对是形容词 vastus 与动词 vastare，都与空旷和毁坏有关。

items.example: It shows the old root in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语里展示这个老词根。

definition_zh: 拱顶；穹窿；地下室；金库；墓室；跳跃；撑杆跳
definition_en: an arched ceiling or a room covered by one, a secure underground room, or a leap over something
core_image: 弧形石顶从两侧墙脚上升，在正中交会；地面之下另有一间锁着的石室，走廊尽头则有人撑杆跃过横杆
scene: 教堂中殿上方的石顶由两侧墙脚起弧，在正中交会。The vault above the nave has carried the roof for eight centuries.
sceneCN: 这里 vault 指「覆盖空间的拱形顶棚」（第 1 个义项：拱顶、穹窿）；句意为中殿上方的拱顶已承住屋顶八个世纪。图中可辨识物件：弧形石顶、两侧墙脚、中殿、屋顶。

pos.zh: 拱顶；穹窿；地下室；金库；墓室
跳跃越过；撑杆跳

derivatives.zh: 拱形的；有拱顶的
拱顶结构；跳跃
撑杆跳运动员
撑杆跳项目
拱顶般的

senses.title: An arched ceiling
senses.definition: a ceiling formed by an arch or a series of arches
senses.definitionCN: 由一道拱或一系列拱构成的顶棚
senses.example: The barrel vault runs the whole length of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 筒形拱顶贯通整条走廊。
senses.why: the word came from a Latin term for something rolled or turned, and an arch turned over a space is exactly that shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「卷、转」的说法，而绕空间翻转的拱正是那种形状。

senses.title: The space under a vault
senses.definition: a room or passage roofed by an arch
senses.definitionCN: 由拱顶覆盖的房间或通道
senses.example: The vault under the choir is open to visitors in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗席下方的拱顶空间夏季向访客开放。
senses.why: a roof and the room it covers are so closely joined that one word names both.
senses.whyCN: 屋顶与其覆盖的房间结合得太紧，于是一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: An underground storage room
senses.definition: a secure room below ground, often bricked or stone-lined
senses.definitionCN: 地下安全房间，常以砖石砌成
senses.example: The wine vault stays at a constant twelve degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 酒窖常年保持十二度。
senses.why: stone-lined cellars were built with arched roofs, so the roof word became the room word.
senses.whyCN: 石砌地窖多用拱形顶，因此屋顶词变成房间词。

senses.title: A bank's strong room
senses.definition: a heavily protected room where money and valuables are kept
senses.definitionCN: 存放金钱与贵重物品的强力防护房间
senses.example: The bank vault opens only with two separate keys.
senses.exampleCN: 银行金库只有用两把不同的钥匙才能打开。
senses.why: security borrowed the cellar's solidity, and the word now suggests steel and locks rather than stone.
senses.whyCN: 保安借用了地窖的坚固感，这个词如今让人想到钢与锁，而非石头。

senses.title: A family burial chamber
senses.definition: a stone room beneath a church or in a cemetery used for burials
senses.definitionCN: 教堂之下或墓地中用于安葬的石室
senses.example: Three generations are buried in the vault under the chapel.
senses.exampleCN: 有三代人葬在小教堂下的墓室里。
senses.why: the underground arched room was a natural place for the dead, so the word acquired a funerary sense.
senses.whyCN: 地下的拱形房间很适合安置死者，因此这个词获得了丧葬义。

senses.title: A crypt beneath a church
senses.definition: the vaulted chamber under the main altar of a church
senses.definitionCN: 教堂主祭坛下的拱顶房间
senses.example: The crypt vault was dug in the eleventh century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座地下墓室建于十一世纪。
senses.why: church building gave the underground room a precise liturgical place and name.
senses.whyCN: 教堂建筑赋予地下房间一个精确的礼仪位置与名称。

senses.title: A leap over an obstacle
senses.definition: a jump made with the hands or a pole, especially over something
senses.definitionCN: 用手或杆完成的跳跃，尤指越过某物
senses.example: He cleared the fence with a single vault.
senses.exampleCN: 他一跃就越过了围栏。
senses.why: this sense came through a different French verb meaning to turn or tumble, and a turning body is a leaping body.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个法语动词，意为翻转或翻滚，而翻转的身体正是跳跃的身体。

senses.title: The pole vault event
senses.definition: the athletics event in which an athlete clears a bar with a long pole
senses.definitionCN: 运动员用长杆越过横杆的田径项目
senses.example: She set the national record in the vault last season.
senses.exampleCN: 上个赛季她在撑杆跳项目上刷新了全国纪录。
senses.why: the event name is the leap noun narrowed into a sport with rules and a bar.
senses.whyCN: 项目名是把跳跃名词收窄为有规则与横杆的运动。

intro.en: Vault is two senses from one Latin rolling root: a turned roof and a turned body. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vault 的两个义项同出一个拉丁语「滚动」词根：翻转的屋顶与翻转的身体。年代均为约数。

items.en: Volvere meant to roll, turn or wrap around, and it supplied a family of words about curved and rolling motion.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚动、转动或缠绕，衍生出一族关于曲线与滚动运动的词。

items.en: Voluta named a spiral or scroll shape, and it described the curled capital of a column.
items.cn: voluta 指螺旋或涡卷形状，也描述柱头的卷曲。

items.en: A later form named a turn or an arched covering, and Old French voute carried the roof sense to English.
items.cn: 后期形式指转弯或拱形覆盖，古法语 voute 把屋顶义带入英语。

items.en: A related verb meant to turn or tumble, and its English descendant gave the leap sense.
items.cn: 一个相关动词意为翻转或翻滚，其英语后裔给出了跳跃义。

items.en: Romanesque and Gothic masons made the vault a structural system, and the word followed stone, cellar and tomb.
items.cn: 罗曼式与哥特式石匠把拱顶发展成结构体系，这个词随石头、地窖与墓室延伸。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin ancestry of volvere is not settled, and the Indo-European root commonly proposed for it is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：volvere 在拉丁语之前的谱系尚无定论，通常为其提出的印欧语词根是重构形式，而非有记录的形式。

note.en: Group one holds curved-roof words and easily confused forms; group two holds secure rooms and jumping words.
note.cn: 第一组是曲面屋顶词与易混形式；第二组是安全房间与跳跃词。

entries.definition: Having a vault; it describes a building rather than naming the roof.
entries.definitionCN: 有拱顶的；描述建筑，而非命名屋顶。

entries.definition: A spiral scroll on an Ionic capital, from the same Latin rolling root.
entries.definitionCN: 爱奥尼柱头上的螺旋涡卷，同出拉丁「滚动」词根。

entries.definition: The unit of electrical force, named after an Italian scientist; it has no connection to the roof word.
entries.definitionCN: 电动势单位，以意大利科学家命名，与屋顶词无关。

entries.definition: It can mean either the building of vaults or the act of leaping; context decides which.
entries.definitionCN: 既指建造拱顶，也指跳跃动作，由语境决定。

entries.definition: A rounded roof over a circular space; a vault is usually arched along a line or a grid.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖圆形空间的圆顶；拱顶通常沿一条线或网格起拱。

entries.definition: A stone chamber beneath a church, usually for burial; it often has a vault but need not.
entries.definitionCN: 教堂下的石室，通常用于安葬；常有拱顶，但非必需。

entries.definition: An underground storage room, usually for wine or goods; it is plainer than the secure vault.
entries.definitionCN: 地下储藏室，通常存酒或货物；比强调安全性的 vault 朴素。

entries.definition: A jump, often a long one; vault is a leap over an obstacle or with a pole.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指跳跃，常指远跳；vault 是越过障碍或以杆完成的跳。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real rolling root, the real building terms and the real athletics event.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「滚动」词根、真实的建筑术语与真实的田径项目。

normal.en: One root means roll or turn: a turned roof and a turning body gave the two main senses.
normal.cn: 同一个词根意为滚动或转动：翻转的屋顶与翻转的身体给出两个主要义项。

normal.en: The family runs vault, vaulted, vaulting, vaulter, pole vault, vault-like.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 vault、vaulted、vaulting、vaulter、pole vault、vault-like。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: barrel vault, ribbed vault, bank vault, burial vault, pole vault.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：筒形拱顶、肋拱顶、银行金库、家族墓室、撑杆跳。

normal.en: A stone roof over a cellar became the word for the cellar and then for a bank's strong room.
normal.cn: 地窖上的石顶先成为地窖之名，再成为银行金库之名。

normal.en: The gymnastics sense keeps the turning body, not the stone.
normal.cn: 跳跃义保留的是翻转的身体，而非石头。

abstract.en: Picture a stone bowl turned upside down and buried halfway.
abstract.cn: 想象一只石碗倒扣过来，一半埋进土里。

abstract.en: Picture a locked room under a church where the only light comes from the door.
abstract.cn: 想象教堂之下一间上锁的屋子，唯一的光来自门口。

abstract.en: Picture a body turning in the air as if rolling over an invisible line.
abstract.cn: 想象一具身体在空中翻转，仿佛越过一条看不见的线。

examples.en: The vault of the nave is held by ribs of cut stone.
examples.cn: 中殿的拱顶由切石肋支撑。

examples.en: The documents were moved to a vault during the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水期间，文件被转移到金库。

examples.en: He vaulted the low wall without breaking stride.
examples.cn: 他一步未停就越过了矮墙。

dict_mnemonic.text: volvere（滚动、翻转）→ 翻转成拱的顶 → 拱顶、地下室、金库；翻转身体 → 跳跃

root: 拉丁 volvere「滚动、翻转」衍生 voluta「涡卷」与后期 volta「拱形覆盖」，经古法语 voute 入英语；跳跃义经古法语 volter「翻转、翻滚」而来。英语 vault。volvere 的更早来源不确定，相关印欧词根属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one turn: a roof turns over a space, the room beneath it becomes a cellar, a strong room and a tomb, while a turning body becomes a leap and a sport.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次翻转展开：屋顶绕空间翻转，其下的房间成为地窖、金库与墓室；而翻转的身体成为跳跃与运动项目。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve rising from two feet and meeting at the middle, and a body turning over a bar.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从两侧墙脚升起、在中间交会的曲线，以及一具越过横杆翻转的身体。

branches.en: THE ROOF: the first sense is the curved ceiling itself.
branches.cn: 屋顶：第一个义项就是曲面顶棚本身。

branches.en: THE ROOM BELOW: a vaulted space and a storage cellar are the roof and the room it shelters.
branches.cn: 其下的房间：拱顶空间与储藏地窖，是屋顶与它所庇护的房间。

branches.en: SECURE DEPTHS: a bank's strong room, a family tomb and a church crypt all turn the underground room into protection.
branches.cn: 安全的地下：银行金库、家族墓室与教堂地下墓室，都把地下房间变成保护。

branches.en: THE TURNED BODY: the leap comes from the same root's idea of turning over.
branches.cn: 翻转的身体：跳跃来自同一词根「翻转」的观念。

branches.en: THE SPORT: the leap is narrowed into an event with a pole and a bar.
branches.cn: 运动：跳跃被收窄为有杆与横杆的项目。

intro.en: Vault comes from a Latin rolling verb, so its affix list follows one root through roof, room and leap.
intro.cn: vault 来自一个拉丁语「滚动」动词，因此其词缀清单沿同一词根贯穿屋顶、房间与跳跃。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and voluta stand behind the roof sense, while the leap sense came through a French verb for turning over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere 与 voluta 支撑屋顶义，而跳跃义经一个表示翻转的法语动词而来。

items.structure: volvere, volvi, volutum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root pictures motion around a centre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘绕中心的运动。

items.example: A voluta curls at the top of a column.

items.meaning: an arched ceiling; a secure room

items.exampleCN: 有拱顶的地窖保持凉爽。

items.meaning: vault construction, or the act of leaping
items.example: Vaulting began with stone and ended in sport.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从石头开始，最后落到运动。

items.example: The vaulter cleared the bar on the third try.
items.exampleCN: 撑杆跳选手第三次越过横杆。

items.meaning: the athletics event of jumping with a pole
items.example: The pole vault needs speed and timing.
items.exampleCN: 撑杆跳需要速度与时机。

definition_zh: 蔬菜；植物（总称，较旧用法）；形容词：植物的、蔬菜的；植物人（口语，多用于 be a vegetable）
definition_en: a plant or part of a plant eaten as food, such as a carrot or cabbage
core_image: 菜篮里横着一根带泥的胡萝卜，叶子还挂着水珠
scene: 厨房案板上摊着刚洗好的青菜、辣椒和番茄，水还在滴。She grows most of her own vegetables in a small garden.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetable 是「蔬菜」（第 1 个义项：可食用的植物或其部分）；句意为她大部分的蔬菜都种在自己的小园子里。菜篮里那根带泥的胡萝卜，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：蔬菜；植物（总称）
形容词：蔬菜的、植物的

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「素食者」，由本词加 -arian 构成
名词，义为「植被、草木」，同源于拉丁语 vegetare「生长」
动词，义为「生长；无所事事地过日子」
形容词，义为「植物的」，较书面

senses.title: Food from plants
senses.titleCN: 蔬菜：可吃的植物或其部分
senses.definition: a plant or part of a plant used as food, such as cabbage or carrot
senses.definitionCN: 可食用的植物或其部分，如甘蓝、胡萝卜
senses.example: She grows most of her own vegetables in a small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她大部分的蔬菜都种在自己的小园子里。
senses.why: Latin vegetare means to grow; a vegetable is simply the part of a growing plant that reaches the table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vegetare 意为生长；蔬菜就是生长中的植物里走上餐桌的那一部分。

senses.title: Plants in general
senses.titleCN: 植物：较旧的总称，常带科学色彩
senses.definition: a plant or plant life in general, in older or scientific writing
senses.definitionCN: 笼统指植物，见于较早或科学性的文字
senses.example: The museum has a large collection of fossils of ancient vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏了大量古代植物的化石。
senses.why: The older sense covers the whole kingdom; the kitchen sense pulled one part of it away.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义覆盖整个界，厨房用法把其中一部分拽了出来。

senses.title: Of plants
senses.titleCN: 植物的：作定语说明来源
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean made from or of plants
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示由植物制成或与植物有关
senses.example: The soup was cooked in vegetable oil rather than butter.
senses.exampleCN: 汤是用植物油而不是黄油煮的。
senses.why: As a modifier the word labels a source, not a kind of plant.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标的是来源，而不是某种植物。

senses.title: A person without response
senses.titleCN: 植物人：口语里形容毫无反应的人
senses.definition: in informal medical talk, a person alive but unable to respond or move
senses.definitionCN: 口语医疗说法，指活着却无法回应或活动的人
senses.example: He was no longer ill, but he lay as a vegetable for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病已不是问题，却像植物人一样躺了多年。
senses.why: The metaphor is blunt: only growth remains, all communication gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很直接：只剩生长，一切交流都消失了。

intro.en: Vegetable comes from Latin vegetabilis, able to grow, from the verb vegetare, to be lively.
intro.cn: vegetable 来自拉丁语 vegetabilis「能生长的」，出自动词 vegetare「有生气、生长」。

items.en: The verb vegere meant to be active or lively, applied to anything growing and powered.
items.cn: 动词 vegere 意为有活力、活跃，用于正在生长、有生机的东西。

items.en: Its frequentative vegetare meant to animate or make grow, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 其反复态 vegetare 意为使有生气、使生长，是整个词族的根。

items.en: The adjective vegetabilis meant capable of growth, applied to plants and soil.
items.cn: 形容词 vegetabilis 意为能生长的，用于植物与土壤。

items.en: Old French used vegetable for anything that grew, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 古法语用 vegetable 指一切会生长之物，英语即以此义借入。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the kitchen sense had pushed the general one aside in daily speech.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，厨房里的用法在日常语言中把笼统的含义挤到了一边。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the grow- family; the near-meaning group holds plant foods and words for plants.
note.cn: 形近组沿「生长」词族；近义组收植物性食物与泛指植物的词。

entries.definition: A person who avoids meat; built on vegetable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「素食者」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: Plant life as a whole, the old general sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「植被」，即较旧的笼统含义。

entries.definition: To grow as a plant, or to live without activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生长」，也指无所事事地活着。

entries.definition: A learned adjective for plant life.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「植物的」，书面色彩。

entries.definition: One common vegetable, with its own round picture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卷心菜」，单一蔬菜，画面自成一格。

entries.definition: The seed-bearing part, a kitchen partner and rival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水果」，含籽的部分，厨房里的伙伴与对手。

entries.definition: Farm products sold together, fruit and vegetables at once.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农产品」，把果蔬一起算。

entries.definition: Plants grown for harvest, seen as a field or yield.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「作物」，从田野与产量的角度看。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the growing-plant root and the kitchen sense that now dominates.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「生长植物」的词根，以及如今占主导的厨房含义。

normal.en: Vegetable comes from a Latin verb meaning to grow.
normal.cn: vegetable 出自一个意为「生长」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Vegetables are eaten; a vegetarian eats no meat.
normal.cn: 蔬菜是吃的，而 vegetarian 是不吃肉的人。

normal.en: Vegetation is the old, wide sense: all of the plants.
normal.cn: vegetation 是旧的宽泛指：所有植物。

normal.en: Vegetable oil is oil pressed from plants, not from butter.
normal.cn: vegetable oil 是从植物压榨的油，不是黄油。

normal.en: A vegetable garden grows food, a flower garden grows beauty.
normal.cn: 菜园种食物，花园种美。

abstract.en: The word once meant anything that grows, and now means what we pick and cook.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指一切会生长之物，如今指我们采摘下锅的东西。

abstract.en: It marks a boundary humans drew, not one nature keeps: tomato is a fruit in botany and a vegetable in the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 它标的是人划的界线而非自然的：番茄在植物学是果实，在厨房是蔬菜。

abstract.en: From life to food to mere survival, the same root covers growth, harvest and the loss of speech.
abstract.cn: 从生命到食物再到只剩生存，同一个词根覆盖成长、收获与失语。

examples.en: Eat more fresh vegetables and less fried food.
examples.cn: 多吃新鲜蔬菜，少吃油炸食物。

examples.en: They planted vegetables behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后种了蔬菜。

examples.en: The dish is cooked with vegetable oil and garlic.
examples.cn: 这道菜用植物油和大蒜烹制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威治特波」——威（为）治特（吃）吧，多吃蔬菜：蔬菜

root: 源自拉丁语 vegetabilis「能生长的」，出自 vegetare「使生长」，经古法语 vegetable 进入英语；同族词有 vegetarian、vegetation、vegetate。

sensesIntro.en: Vegetable moves from the whole plant kingdom to the kitchen, then to a modifier and an old blunt figure of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: vegetable 从整个植物界走进厨房，再成为修饰语，最后化作一句直白的旧比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a muddy carrot from the garden, leaves still beaded with water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根带泥的胡萝卜，叶子还挂着水珠。

branches.en: KITCHEN LINE: the edible part of a plant.
branches.cn: 厨房线：植物可食的部分。

branches.en: BOTANY LINE: the whole plant world, an older use.
branches.cn: 植物学线：整个植物界，较旧用法。

branches.en: LABEL LINE: vegetable oil names a source.
branches.cn: 标签线：vegetable oil 标的是来源。

branches.en: LOSS LINE: life without response, a blunt metaphor.
branches.cn: 丧失线：只剩生命而无反应，直白比喻。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a vegetable is food, vegetable oil is a material.
branches.cn: 对照线：vegetable 是食物，vegetable oil 是原料。

intro.en: Vegetable keeps its Latin adjective ending; English relatives use -arian, -ation and -ate.
intro.cn: vegetable 保留了拉丁形容词词尾，英语亲属词则用 -arian、-ation、-ate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is vegere, vegetare and vegetabilis, all about life and growth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁链条是 vegere、vegetare、vegetabilis，都与生命和生长有关。

items.example: It shows the word as a modifier.

definition_zh: 植被；某一地区全部植物；（医学）赘生物
definition_en: the plant life of an area taken as a whole, especially what covers the ground; in medicine, an abnormal growth on a body surface
core_image: 一片土地被草木密密铺满，从贴地的苔藓一直连到高处的树冠，像一床会呼吸的绿被
scene: 沙丘表面只有薄薄一层草木；风一吹沙就移动，研究员靠记录这层草木的厚薄与种类判断沙丘是否稳定。Thin vegetation holds the dunes together against the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetation 指「一个地区地表全部植物形成的覆盖层」（第 1 个义项：把一地植物整体看待）；句意为稀疏的植被把沙丘粘在一起，抵御风的搬运。

pos.zh: 植被；某一地区的全部植物（不可数）
（医学）赘生物；心瓣膜或体表长出的异常组织

derivatives.zh: 生长；像植物一样过呆板生活
营养生长的；植物状态的
植被的；与植被有关的
长有植被的

senses.title: Collective plant life of a region
senses.titleCN: 一个地区整体看待的植物
senses.definition: the whole body of plants growing in a particular area
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区生长的全部植物
senses.example: The vegetation of the island is mostly low scrub.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的植被以低矮灌丛为主。
senses.why: Vegetation is the noun of state built on vegetare 'to quicken, make lively': wherever plants take hold, the ground is made lively.
senses.whyCN: vegetation 是由表示「使有生气」的 vegetare 加名词后缀构成的状态名词：凡是植物扎下根的地方，土地就活了起来。

senses.title: The ground-covering layer
senses.titleCN: 贴地铺开、护住土壤的那一层
senses.definition: the layer of plants that covers the ground and protects the soil
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖地表并保护土壤的植物层
senses.example: Thin vegetation holds the dunes together against the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 稀疏的植被把沙丘粘在一起，抵御风。
senses.why: The collective sense narrows here to what touches the surface: roots bind grains, stems slow the wind, and the ground stops moving.
senses.whyCN: 整体义在此收窄为「接触地表」的部分：根抓住沙粒，茎挡住风，地面便不再移动。

senses.title: Rank or luxuriant growth
senses.titleCN: 长得过盛、几乎挡住路的草木
senses.definition: plants growing thickly and abundantly in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某地长得繁茂浓密的植物
senses.example: Vegetation grew thick along the irrigation ditch.
senses.exampleCN: 灌渠边的草木长得又密又高。
senses.why: When growth runs ahead of use, the word shifts from what is there to how much of it there is, and the tone becomes almost a complaint.
senses.whyCN: 当生长超出需要，词义就从「有什么」转向「有多少」，语气也近乎抱怨。

senses.title: A plant community or type
senses.titleCN: 按形态划分的一类植物群落
senses.definition: a class of plant community distinguished by its structure and species
senses.definitionCN: 按结构与物种划分出的植物群落类型
senses.example: Botanists classify the valley's vegetation into four formations.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家把谷地的植被分为四个群系。
senses.why: Modern ecology turns the mass noun into a countable technical term: each formation is a named package of species and structure.
senses.whyCN: 现代生态学把这个不可数名词变成可数的术语：每个群系都是物种与结构组成的有名组合。

senses.title: The record made by a survey
senses.titleCN: 调查后绘制出的植被记录
senses.definition: the plants of an area as recorded, mapped or described by a survey
senses.definitionCN: 经调查、绘图或描述记录下来的植被
senses.example: The team finished a vegetation survey before the dam was built.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝动工前，团队完成了植被调查。
senses.why: Surveying fixes the living layer into data, so the same word now names a map, a list and a baseline for later comparison.
senses.whyCN: 调查把这层活的东西固定成资料，同一个词于是既指图，也指清单，还指日后比对的基线。

senses.title: What is cleared away
senses.titleCN: 被当作障碍清理掉的草木
senses.definition: plants regarded as an obstacle and removed from a site
senses.definitionCN: 被视为障碍而从场地清除的植物
senses.example: Workers cleared the vegetation around the new pipeline.
senses.exampleCN: 工人清除了新管线周围的植被。
senses.why: Once plants are in the way of a project, the word stops describing an ecosystem and starts describing material to be removed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦草木挡了工程的路，这个词就不再描述生态系统，而开始指待清除的对象。

senses.title: Abnormal tissue growth
senses.definition: a mass of abnormal tissue, especially on a heart valve or body surface
senses.definitionCN: 异常长出的组织块，尤指心瓣膜或体表上的
senses.example: Echocardiography showed a small vegetation on the valve.
senses.exampleCN: 超声心动图显示瓣膜上有一个小的赘生物。
senses.why: Medical Latin applied the plant-growth word to anything that sprouts where it should not, so the image of unwanted sprouting carries over.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语把这个「植物生长」的词用到一切不该长却长出来的东西上，杂草蔓生的意象因此延续。

senses.title: Plant cover read as a climate record
senses.titleCN: 被当作气候档案来读的植被
senses.definition: past plant cover reconstructed from pollen, seeds or other traces
senses.definitionCN: 从花粉、种子等遗迹重建出的过去植物覆盖
senses.example: Pollen in the lake mud records how the vegetation changed.
senses.exampleCN: 湖泥里的花粉记录了植被如何变化。
senses.why: Because plant cover answers to rainfall and temperature, its fossil traces become a thermometer for ancient climates.
senses.whyCN: 植物覆盖随降水与温度而变，因此它的化石遗迹成了测量古气候的温度计。

intro.en: Vegetation comes from Medieval Latin vegetatio 'a quickening, growth', from vegetare 'to enliven', built on vegetus 'lively'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vegetation 来自中世纪拉丁 vegetatio「使有生气、生长」，源于 vegetare「使有生气」，再往前是 vegetus「有活力的」。年代为约数。

items.en: Vegere meant 'to be lively, active'. Its deeper origin is not settled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: vegere 意为「有生气、活动着」。其更深来源没有定论，凡为它给出的印欧形式都是重构形式。

items.en: The participle vegetus 'lively, vigorous' supplied the adjective from which the verb was felt to come.
items.cn: 分词 vegetus「有活力的、精神抖擞的」提供了形容词，人们也觉得动词正是由它而来。

items.en: Vegetare 'to enliven, animate' produced Medieval Latin vegetatio 'a making lively, growth'.
items.cn: vegetare「使有生气、使活动」产生了中世纪拉丁 vegetatio「使有生气、生长」。

items.en: English adopted vegetation in the seventeenth century for the plant life of a region, and botany fixed it as a technical collective noun.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪借入 vegetation，指一地的植物，植物学随后把它固定为技术性的集合名词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century physicians used vegetation for abnormal growths on valves and surfaces, borrowing the image of something sprouting.
items.cn: 19 世纪起，医生用 vegetation 指瓣膜与体表上的异常生长物，借的是「冒出来生长」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the link of vegere to vigere 'to be vigorous' is generally believed but not demonstrated, and the first English date for the botanical sense is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：vegere 与 vigere「强健」的联系一般认为成立，却未经证实；植物义在英语中的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates look-alikes that share the Latin root from one false friend; group two holds the words used for plant cover in ecology.
note.cn: 第一组区分共用拉丁词根的外形相近词与一个假朋友；第二组是生态学里指植物覆盖的近义词。

entries.definition: From vegetare, but in English it means to live a dull, inactive life or, of plants, simply to grow.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 vegetare，但在英语里指过呆板无所事事的生活，或指植物生长。

entries.definition: From Latin vegetabilis 'animating', the same root, but the noun settled on a garden crop.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vegetabilis「有生气的」，词根相同，名词却落在园圃作物上。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'of plants' or 'plant-like', closer to the Latin source than vegetation is.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「植物的、像植物的」，比 vegetation 更贴近拉丁原义。

entries.definition: From venerari 'to worship', with no plant meaning at all; only the sound overlaps.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 venerari「敬拜」，与植物无关，只有读音重叠。

entries.definition: The plant species of a region listed by name; vegetation is the living cover itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个地区按名称列出的植物物种；vegetation 指活生生的覆盖本身。

entries.definition: Green plants seen as pleasant colour; it is a look, while vegetation is an ecological mass.
entries.definitionCN: 把绿色植物当作悦目的颜色；它说的是一种外观，vegetation 说的是生态整体。

entries.definition: A neutral everyday phrase with no technical edge; vegetation is its scientific counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的日常说法，不带技术色彩；vegetation 是它的科学对应词。

entries.definition: The total mass of living material, measured by weight; vegetation names the cover, not the weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指活物质的总质量，按重量计；vegetation 指覆盖，不指重量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin family and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的拉丁词族与真实搭配，不编顺口溜。

normal.en: vegetare 'to enliven' + -ation: the state of ground made lively by plants.
normal.cn: vegetare「使有生气」+ -ation：土地被植物弄得有生气的状态。

normal.en: The family: vegetate, vegetative, vegetational, vegetated.
normal.cn: 同族：vegetate、vegetative、vegetational、vegetated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: natural vegetation, dense vegetation, sparse vegetation, native vegetation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：天然植被、茂密植被、稀疏植被、乡土植被。

normal.en: The same root gives vegetable and vegetal, both about plant life.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 vegetable 与 vegetal，都与植物有关。

normal.en: Medical charts speak of a vegetation on a valve, a sprout where nothing should sprout.
normal.cn: 病历上说瓣膜上有赘生物，即在不该长的地方长出一块。

abstract.en: Picture a lawn so thick that you cannot see the soil beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片厚到看不见下面泥土的草坪。

abstract.en: Picture a green blanket laid over a wound in the land.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绿毯盖在土地的伤口上。

abstract.en: Picture a library shelf where every plant of a valley is filed as one volume.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上有一卷书，把一个谷地的植物全归档在里面。

examples.en: Fires every few years keep the vegetation short and diverse.
examples.cn: 每隔几年烧一次，植被就保持低矮而多样。

examples.en: Loose vegetation was cleared before the foundations were poured.
examples.cn: 浇筑地基之前，松散的植被已被清除。

examples.en: The valley's vegetation shifts from grass to oak as you climb.
examples.cn: 沿山坡向上，谷地植被从草类变为橡树。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维基（veget）+ 生长（ation）」——地上长满绿色档案 → 植被

root: 拉丁 vegetare「使有生气、促使生长」＝ vegere「有活力」＋反复后缀；vegetatio 指「生长」。vegere 更深来源不确定，与 vigere「强健」的联系一般认为成立但未证实。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is made lively, the ground is covered, the cover is classified, mapped, cleared, and finally read either as disease or as climate.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先使某处有生气，再铺满地面，然后被分类、绘图、清除，最后或被读成疾病，或被读成气候。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a living quilt spread over the ground, growing from below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一床铺在地面上的活被子，从下面长上来。

branches.en: QUICKENING: the root sense is making a place lively, whether mildly or rankly.
branches.cn: 使有生气：词根义就是让某处活起来，无论温和还是过盛。

branches.en: COVER: roots bind the surface, so the mass becomes a protective layer.
branches.cn: 覆盖：根抓住地表，整体于是成为保护层。

branches.en: CLASSIFY: ecology names formations, then fixes them into surveys.
branches.cn: 分类：生态学先给群系命名，再把它们固定为调查资料。

branches.en: OBSTACLE: what blocks a project turns from ecosystem into material to be removed.
branches.cn: 障碍：挡住工程的部分，从生态系统变成待清材料。

branches.en: TWO READINGS: growth may be disease in a body or evidence of ancient climate in mud.
branches.cn: 两种读法：生长既可能是体内的病，也可能是泥里的古气候证据。

intro.en: Vegetation is built from a Latin verb stem plus a noun suffix, and that stem also builds several everyday English words.
intro.cn: vegetation 由拉丁动词词干加名词后缀构成，这个词干还构成若干日常英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vegere 'to be lively' gives vegetus, vegetare, vegetatio; the suffix -ation marks an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vegere「有生气」给出 vegetus、vegetare、vegetatio；后缀 -ation 表示动作或其结果。

items.example: The bare stem carries the idea of life.
items.exampleCN: 光秃的词干带着「活」的意思。

items.example: The adjective describes ground that is full of growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述长满植物的土地。

items.example: Warm rain vegetates the dry slope.
The noun names the process, not the plants.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指过程，不指植物。

items.meaning: action or result of an action
items.example: It turns a verb stem into a nameable state.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词词干变成可命名的状态。

items.meaning: the state of ground made lively
to grow, or to live dully
items.example: Moss vegetates on the shaded wall.
items.exampleCN: 苔藓在背阴的墙上生长。

items.meaning: tending to grow rather than reproduce

items.example: The vegetated bank held the soil.
items.exampleCN: 长满植物的河岸保住了土壤。

definition_zh: 车辆；交通工具；（思想、信息的）传播媒介、手段；载体
definition_en: a machine with wheels or an engine used for transport, or a means of expressing something
core_image: 一辆车停在站台边，门一开，车上的人和想法一起下车
scene: 早高峰的马路上一排车缓缓挪动，尾灯连成一条红线。No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
sceneCN: 这里 vehicle 是「车辆」（第 1 个义项：有轮或有发动机的运输工具）；句意为这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。站台边停着的那辆车，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：车辆、交通工具；传播媒介、手段；载体

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「车辆的、车辆使用的」
名词短语，义为「车辆交通」

senses.title: A machine for transport
senses.titleCN: 车辆：能载人载货的机器
senses.definition: a machine with wheels or an engine used to carry people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 有轮或发动机、用来载人或载货的机器
senses.example: No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。
senses.why: Latin vehiculum named a plain means of carrying, and the road sense grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vehiculum 原指一种朴素的「搬运手段」，道路上的含义由此长出来。

senses.title: A means of expression
senses.titleCN: 表达手段：让思想能走动的载体
senses.definition: a way or medium through which ideas or feelings are expressed
senses.definitionCN: 使思想或感情得以表达的方式或媒介
senses.example: The novel served as a vehicle for her views on education.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说成了她表达教育观点的载体。
senses.why: What carries goods also carries ideas; the word moves from wheels to words.
senses.whyCN: 能载货的东西也能载思想；这个词从车轮走到了文字。

senses.title: A medium of transmission
senses.titleCN: 传播媒介：把信息或物质送到别处
senses.definition: a substance or channel that carries something to another place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物带到别处的物质或渠道
senses.example: Water is a common vehicle for disease in crowded cities.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的城市里，水常是疾病的传播媒介。
senses.why: The word is neutral about what is carried: people, ideas or germs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对载着什么保持中立：可以是人、思想或病菌。

senses.title: A medium in art and science
senses.titleCN: 溶剂、调色媒介：科学艺术里承载别物的东西
senses.definition: a liquid in which a substance is carried, as in paint or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 承载其他物质的液体，如颜料或药物里的媒介
senses.example: The pigments are held in an oil vehicle before the paint dries.
senses.exampleCN: 颜料在干之前由油性媒介承载。
senses.why: In a workshop the word returns to its plainest sense: something liquid does the carrying.
senses.whyCN: 在作坊里，这个词回到最朴素的意思：由一种液体来承担搬运。

intro.en: Vehicle comes from Latin vehiculum, a means of carrying, built from the verb vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: vehicle 来自拉丁语 vehiculum「搬运手段」，出自动词 vehere「运载」。

items.en: The verb vehere meant to carry or convey, said of riders, ships and carts.
items.cn: 动词 vehere 意为运载，用于骑手、船只和车。

items.en: Its noun vehiculum named any means of transport, not only a machine.
items.cn: 其名词 vehiculum 指任何运输手段，不只是机器。

items.en: French kept véhicule for carts and carriages, and English borrowed that sense.
items.cn: 法语保留 véhicule 指车马，英语借入的就是这一含义。

items.en: With the motor car the street sense tightened into vehicles on wheels.
items.cn: 随着汽车出现，日常含义收窄为带轮子的车辆。

items.en: At the same time the older sense of a carrier widened again into ideas and media.
items.cn: 与此同时，「承载物」的旧义又扩展开来，用于思想与媒介。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the veh- carrying stem; the near-meaning group holds transport words and carriers.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「运载」的 veh- 词干；近义组收交通与承载相关的词。

entries.definition: Of or for vehicles; the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「车辆的」，是本词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: A blood vessel; sounds close but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「血管」，音近但不同根。

entries.definition: To carry something across; formed with con-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「运送、传达」，同一拉丁词根加 con-。

entries.definition: A journey by sea; from the same carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航行」，出自同一个运载动词。

entries.definition: A passenger road vehicle, the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小汽车」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The whole system of moving people and goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运输」，指整套运送系统。

entries.definition: A channel for ideas or messages, the abstract sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「媒介」，即抽象的含义。

entries.definition: One that carries, used of people, bags or germs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「携带者」，用于人、袋子或病菌。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the carrying root and the double life of the word as transport and as medium.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「运载」词根，以及这个词作为交通工具与媒介的双重身份。

normal.en: Vehicle comes from a Latin verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: vehicle 出自一个意为「运载」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Motor vehicle is the formal term in law and insurance.
normal.cn: motor vehicle 是法律与保险里的正式说法。

normal.en: A vehicle for change is a means, not a machine.
normal.cn: a vehicle for change 指手段，不是机器。

normal.en: Convey and voyage share the same root as vehicle.
normal.cn: convey 与 voyage 和 vehicle 同根。

normal.en: The plural is vehicles, with the k sound kept before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 vehicles，k 音在 s 前仍然保留。

abstract.en: Everything in the word is about being carried: a body, an idea, a germ, a colour.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的全是「被载着」：身体、想法、病菌、颜色。

abstract.en: A vehicle changes the reach of what it carries; the idea is the same size, the audience is not.
abstract.cn: 交通工具改变的是所载之物的抵达范围；想法没变大，听众变大了。

abstract.en: The oldest sense was any means; modern life narrowed it to wheels and then quietly reopened it.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义是任何手段；现代生活把它收窄到车轮，又悄悄打开。

examples.en: All vehicles must stop at the red light.
examples.cn: 所有车辆必须在红灯前停下。

examples.en: The film became a vehicle for young actors.
examples.cn: 这部电影成了年轻演员展示自己的载体。

examples.en: Mosquitoes are a vehicle for several diseases.
examples.cn: 蚊子是几种疾病的传播媒介。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为爱扣」——为爱扣上车门，一路载着走：车辆

root: 源自拉丁语名词 vehiculum「运输手段」（动词 vehere「运载」），经法语 véhicule 进入英语；同族词有 convey、voyage、vehicular。

sensesIntro.en: Vehicle begins as anything that carries, narrows to cars, then widens back to ideas, germs and paint.
sensesIntro.cn: vehicle 起初指一切运载之物，收窄为车辆，又扩回思想、病菌与颜料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart at the platform, doors open, passengers and their plans getting off together.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台边的一辆车，门一开，乘客和他们的计划一起下来。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: machines with wheels or engines.
branches.cn: 道路线：有轮或发动机的机器。

branches.en: ART LINE: a story that carries a point of view.
branches.cn: 艺术线：承载观点的小说或影片。

branches.en: CHANNEL LINE: water or insects carrying disease.
branches.cn: 渠道线：带病的水或昆虫。

branches.en: PAINT LINE: the liquid that holds pigment.
branches.cn: 颜料线：承载颜料的媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: transport is the system, a vehicle is one machine in it.
branches.cn: 对照线：transport 是系统，vehicle 是其中一台机器。

intro.en: Vehicle is a Latin noun; its relatives mostly come from the same carrying verb with other prefixes.
intro.cn: vehicle 是拉丁名词，亲属词多由同一运载动词加不同前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vehere, to carry, giving vehiculum and also vector and convehere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vehere「运载」，派生出 vehiculum，也派生出 vector 与 convehere。

items.example: It is the core of vehicle.
It names the thing that carries.
It is the same journey idea.
items.exampleCN: 它带有同样的旅程观念。

definition_zh: 静脉；叶脉；矿脉；（言行的）风格，一丝（气质）
definition_en: a tube that carries blood back to the heart, or a narrow streak running through a leaf, through rock, or through a person's manner
core_image: 一根青蓝色细管从指尖蜿蜒回到心脏，同时像叶脉、矿脉那样不断分叉
scene: 这里指「静脉」。 The nurse found a blue vein on the back of his hand and slid the needle in.
sceneCN: 这里 vein 指「皮下可见的静脉」（第 2 个义项：透过皮肤能看到、可用于进针的青蓝色血管）；句意：护士在他手背上找到一根青色的静脉，把针扎了进去。图中可辨识物件：手背、青蓝色血管、输液针、止血带。

pos.zh: 静脉；叶脉；（昆虫）翅脉；矿脉；水脉；（言行的）风格，一丝（气质）
使…带有纹理（罕用）

collocations.zh: 以同样的风格；顺着同一思路

derivatives.zh: 静脉的；静脉中的
小静脉
有纹理的；布满静脉的
静脉内的；静脉注射的
脉序；（叶、翅的）脉纹分布

senses.title: Blood-return vessel
senses.titleCN: 静脉：把血送回心脏的血管
senses.definition: a tube in the body that carries blood from the organs and tissues back to the heart
senses.definitionCN: 体内把血液从器官与组织送回心脏的血管
senses.example: The surgeon tied off the vein to stop the bleeding.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生结扎了那条静脉来止血。
senses.why: Latin vena named any narrow channel, and anatomy kept it for the channel that returns blood, the counterpart of the artery that sends it out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vena 泛指各种狭窄的通道，解剖学沿用它来指「把血送回」的那条通道，与向外送血的动脉相对。

senses.title: Blue line under the skin
senses.titleCN: 皮下可见的青筋：透过皮肤能看到的静脉
senses.definition: a vein that can be seen as a bluish line through the skin and is commonly used for drawing blood or giving a drip
senses.definitionCN: 透过皮肤呈青蓝色、常用于抽血或输液的静脉
senses.example: The nurse found a blue vein on the back of his hand and slid the needle in.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在他手背上找到一根青色的静脉，把针扎了进去。
senses.why: Because veins lie close to the surface and carry dark, oxygen-poor blood, they show through the skin as blue lines, and medicine learned to use them as ready access points.
senses.whyCN: 静脉靠近体表、又携带缺氧的暗色血，因此透过皮肤呈现青蓝色；医学便把它们当作现成的进针口。

senses.title: Leaf vein
senses.titleCN: 叶脉：贯穿叶片、输送水分与养分的脉纹
senses.definition: one of the strands of tissue that run through a leaf and carry water, minerals and sugar
senses.definitionCN: 贯穿叶片、输送水分、矿物质与糖分的条状组织
senses.example: The leaf's veins form a net that carries water to every edge.
senses.exampleCN: 这片叶子的叶脉构成一张网，把水送到每一个边缘。
senses.why: The branching lines of a leaf look exactly like the branching vessels of a body, so botany borrowed the same word for them.
senses.whyCN: 叶片上分叉的线条与体内分叉的血管形状相同，植物学便把同一个词借去指叶脉。

senses.title: Ore seam in rock
senses.titleCN: 矿脉：岩层中呈条带状分布的矿物
senses.definition: a layer or streak of mineral, such as gold or copper, running through surrounding rock
senses.definitionCN: 金、铜等矿物在周围岩石中呈层状或条带状的分布
senses.example: Miners followed the gold vein deep into the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工顺着金矿脉一路深入山体。
senses.why: A seam of ore is a thin channel of one substance inside another, the same geometry as a blood vessel, and the word was extended to mining in the Middle Ages.
senses.whyCN: 矿脉是一种物质在另一种物质内部形成的细窄通道，与血管的几何形状相同，这个词在中世纪被延伸到采矿业。

senses.title: Underground water channel
senses.titleCN: 水脉：地下汇流的细窄水道
senses.definition: a narrow underground course along which water flows or collects, often sought when digging a well
senses.definitionCN: 地下水流动或聚积的细窄通道，打井时常被寻找
senses.example: The old well was dug where a water vein ran close to the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 那口老井挖在水脉接近地表的地方。
senses.why: Water moving through soil also follows a narrow line, a sense Latin vena already carried alongside the blood-vessel one.
senses.whyCN: 水在土中流动同样沿一条窄线，拉丁 vena 在指血管之外本就带有这个义项。

senses.title: Manner or tone
senses.titleCN: 风格、口吻：延续同一种写法或说法
senses.definition: a particular style or manner of speaking or writing, especially when something continues in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作的特定风格，尤指顺着同一种方式继续
senses.example: She told a few more jokes in the same vein.
senses.exampleCN: 她又讲了几个同一路数的笑话。
senses.why: A vein runs continuously through a body without breaking, so speech that keeps one tone is imagined as one unbroken line of the same material.
senses.whyCN: 静脉在体内连续不断，于是保持同一基调的言语被想象成一条不中断的同质线条。

senses.title: A streak of a quality
senses.titleCN: 一丝（气质）：性格或作品里隐约的一层
senses.definition: a small but noticeable amount of a quality, such as sadness or humour, in a person or a work
senses.definitionCN: 一个人或一部作品中隐约可辨的一层气质，如忧伤或幽默
senses.example: There is a vein of melancholy in his early poems.
senses.exampleCN: 他的早期诗作里有一丝忧郁。
senses.why: The mining sense supplies the picture: a thin layer of one substance is found inside another, so a thin layer of feeling is found inside a character.
senses.whyCN: 采矿义提供了画面：一种物质以薄层夹在另一种物质里，于是某种情绪也以薄层夹在性格之中。

senses.title: Insect wing vein
senses.titleCN: 翅脉：昆虫翅膀上起支撑作用的脉纹
senses.definition: one of the stiff ribs that support an insect's wing and carry its hemolymph
senses.definitionCN: 支撑昆虫翅膀并输送血淋巴的坚硬脉纹
senses.example: Biologists count the veins in a fly's wing to identify the species.
senses.exampleCN: 生物学家数苍蝇翅膀上的翅脉来鉴定物种。
senses.why: Insect wings repeat the branching-tube pattern, and entomology reused the anatomical word for these ribs in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 昆虫翅膀重复了分叉管道这一图案，昆虫学在 18 世纪把解剖学的这个词用来指这些脉纹。

intro.en: Vein comes from Latin vena through Old French veine. Latin already used the one word for a blood vessel, a water course and a seam of ore, and English copied all three.
intro.cn: vein 经古法语 veine 来自拉丁 vena。拉丁语本就用同一个词指血管、水道与矿脉，英语把这三层一并继承了下来。

items.en: Latin vena meant a blood vessel, and by extension a channel of water and a seam of metal in the earth; the shared picture is a narrow passage inside a larger body.
items.cn: 拉丁 vena 指血管，并引申为水道与地层中的金属脉；共同的画面是「较大物体内部的一条窄通道」。

items.en: Old French veine carried the anatomical sense into English around the fourteenth century, at first mainly as a medical term.
items.cn: 古法语 veine 大约在 14 世纪把解剖义带入英语，起初主要作为医学术语。

items.en: By the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries the word was routine in mining and well-digging, where a vein of ore or water was followed like a line on a map.
items.cn: 到 15、16 世纪，这个词在采矿与打井中已很常用，矿脉或水脉被当作地图上的一条线来追踪。

items.en: Naturalists of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries extended vein to the strands of a leaf and later to the ribs of an insect wing, because the shapes are visibly the same.
items.cn: 17、18 世纪的博物学家把 vein 延伸到叶脉，后来又用于昆虫翅脉，因为这些形状肉眼可见地相同。

items.en: The figurative sense 'tone, style, a strain of feeling' appears in the sixteenth century and survives mainly in the fixed phrase in the same vein.
items.cn: 「口吻、风格、一丝情绪」的比喻义出现于 16 世纪，今天主要存活在「同一口吻」这一固定搭配中。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the deeper origin of Latin vena is unknown, and no Indo-European root is generally accepted for it, so none is reconstructed here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：拉丁 vena 的更早来源不明，学界没有公认的印欧词根，此处不作重构。

note.en: The first group holds sound-alikes and close relatives whose spelling or meaning is easily confused; the second holds words for tubes, seams and streaks that overlap with vein.
note.cn: 第一组是同音或形近、容易混淆的词与近亲；第二组是与 vein 语义重叠的「管道、矿层、条痕」类词。

entries.definition: Means 'too proud' or 'useless'; it comes from Latin vanus 'empty', not from vena.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「自负的」或「徒劳的」，来自拉丁 vanus「空的」，与 vena 无关。

entries.definition: A flat blade that shows wind direction, from an Old English word for a banner; unrelated to the blood vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 指示风向的扁平叶片，来自古英语中表「旗帜」的词，与血管无关。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of the veins'; it describes the vessel rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「静脉的」的形容词，描述血管而不命名血管。

entries.definition: A very small vein; the diminutive suffix marks it as narrower than a vein.
entries.definitionCN: 指小静脉；小称后缀表明它比 vein 更细。

entries.definition: A tube that carries blood away from the heart; vein is the return route, so the two are defined by direction.
entries.definitionCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管；vein 是回流路线，两者靠方向区分。

entries.definition: The thinnest blood vessel, where exchange happens; veins collect what capillaries have exchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 最细的血管，物质交换在此发生；静脉收集毛细血管交换后的血液。

entries.definition: A rich seam of ore in rock, the mining sense of vein without the anatomical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石中富集的矿层，只保留 vein 的采矿义，不含解剖义。

entries.definition: A long thin mark or an element in a character; it overlaps the figurative sense of vein but has no medical use.
entries.definitionCN: 指细长的痕迹或性格中的一种成分，与 vein 的比喻义重叠，但没有医学用法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: English took one Latin word, vena, and kept all three of its senses: vessel, ore seam and water course.
normal.cn: 英语只取了拉丁一个词 vena，却把它指血管、矿脉、水脉的三层意思全都保留下来。

normal.en: The family runs vein, venous, venule, venation and intravenous on the same stem.
normal.cn: 同族词 vein、venous、venule、venation、intravenous 共用同一个词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: jugular vein, portal vein, pulmonary vein.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖位置：颈静脉、门静脉、肺静脉。

normal.en: in the same vein keeps the picture of one continuous streak of talk.
normal.cn: 「同一口吻」这一搭配保留了「一条连续不断的话语线条」这一画面。

normal.en: a vein of humour borrows the miner's sense: a thin layer found inside something else.
normal.cn: 「一丝幽默」这一搭配借用了矿工的义项：夹在其他东西里的一薄层。

abstract.en: Picture an underground river that shows itself only as one blue line under the skin.
abstract.cn: 想象一条地下河，只在皮肤下露出一条青蓝色的线。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf held up to a lamp, its veins like a map of small rivers.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子对着灯举起，叶脉像一张小河的地图。

abstract.en: Picture a miner following a thin gold line through grey rock.
abstract.cn: 想象矿工沿灰色岩石中的一条细金线向前走。

examples.en: Varicose veins often appear after years of standing at work.
examples.cn: 静脉曲张常常在多年站立工作之后出现。

examples.en: The rock face was cut by a wide white vein of quartz.
examples.cn: 岩壁被一条宽阔的白色石英矿脉切开。

examples.en: He answered in a lighter vein than the earlier interview.
examples.cn: 他回答的口吻比先前那次采访轻松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vein 与 vain、vane 同音」——同音词要分清：血管是 vein，徒劳是 vain，风向标是 vane → vein 静脉

root: 拉丁 vena「血管；矿脉；水道」→ 古法语 veine → 英语 vein；拉丁 vena 更早来源不明。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one narrow channel: a tube returning blood, the blue line it makes under the skin, the same shape in a leaf, in rock, in water, in a manner of speech, in a streak of character, and in an insect's wing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条窄通道展开：把血送回心脏的管道、它在皮肤下形成的青蓝线，以及它在叶、岩石、水、说话方式、性格层次和昆虫翅膀上的同形延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow channel that branches through a body, a leaf or stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条在身体、叶片或石头中分叉延伸的窄通道。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND ITS BLUE LINE: the anatomical vessel, then the same vessel as it appears through the skin.
branches.cn: 管道与青蓝线：先是解剖学上的血管，再是它透过皮肤显现的样子。

branches.en: NATURAL BRANCHING: leaves and insect wings repeat the same pattern of fine ribs.
branches.cn: 自然分叉：叶片与昆虫翅膀重复了同样的细脉图案。

branches.en: UNDER THE GROUND: ore seams and water courses are followed like lines on a map.
branches.cn: 地面之下：矿脉与水脉被当作地图上的线来追踪。

branches.en: ONE CONTINUOUS TONE: talk that keeps one style is imagined as an unbroken vein.
branches.cn: 一条不断的语调：保持同一风格的言说被想象成一条不中断的脉。

branches.en: A LAYER INSIDE A PERSON: the mining sense becomes a thin layer of feeling in a character.
branches.cn: 人身上的一层：采矿义转化为性格中薄薄的一层情绪。

intro.en: Vein is a bare Latin stem, vena, with almost no affixation in English; its relatives grow by suffixes such as -ous, -ule and intra-.
intro.cn: vein 是裸露的拉丁词干 vena，英语中几乎没有附加词缀；它的同族词靠 -ous、-ule、intra- 等词缀生长。

latinIntro.en: Latin vena and its adjective venosus, with the diminutive venula, supply the whole English family, including medical compounds built with intra-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vena 及其形容词 venosus、小称 venula 提供了整个英语词族，包括用 intra- 构成的医学复合词。

items.example: The needle went into a vein.
Venous blood returns to the right side of the heart.
A venule drains into a larger vein.
items.exampleCN: 小静脉汇入更大的静脉。

items.meaning: the pattern of veins in a leaf or wing
items.meaningCN: 叶脉或翅脉的分布格局
items.example: The venation of the leaf is net-like.
items.exampleCN: 这片叶子的脉序呈网状。

items.meaning: a small vein of a leaf
items.example: Water reaches the edge along tiny veinlets.
items.exampleCN: 水沿着细小叶脉到达叶缘。

latinEntries.meaning: a blood vessel; a water course; a seam of ore

definition_zh: 速度；速率；速度矢量；快速；周转速度
definition_en: the speed of something in a given direction, or the rate at which something moves or changes
core_image: 一支箭离弦后，箭头旁画着一条带箭头的直线，线上标着等距刻度
scene: 实验台上，小车沿倾斜导轨滑下，两道光门依次亮起，计时器记下通过的时刻。The sensor measured the cart's velocity as it passed each gate.
sceneCN: 这里 velocity 指物体在某一方向上的运动快慢（第 1 个义项：带方向的速度矢量）；句意：传感器测出小车经过每道光门时的速度。图中可辨识物件：倾斜导轨、小车、光门、计时器。

pos.zh: 速度；速率；速度矢量；快速；周转速度
